scope: Exploratory literature synthesis and a local exact graph/geometry probe. No new fundamental theory or physical detection is claimed.

sources.title: Probing Ultralight Bosons with Binary Black Holes
sources.locator: Section 2.2, equations 2.3-2.13; Section 3 on binary-induced transitions
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; relevant equations and surrounding discussion read
sources.supports: Small-alpha gravitational scalar bound states reduce to a Coulomb Schrodinger problem; higher-order splitting and horizon growth/decay break exact hydrogen equivalence.
sources.limits: Does not establish existence of ultralight bosons or observation of an astrophysical cloud. Equating the leading differential equation does not equate quantum statistics or boundary conditions.

sources.title: Schrodinger Evolution of Self-Gravitating Disks
sources.locator: Section 2, equations 1-7; Section 3.2 and its local-coupling assumptions
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; Hamiltonian-to-complex-amplitude derivation and applicability discussion read
sources.supports: Conservative classical inclination dynamics of thin quasi-Keplerian disks admit Schrodinger-form evolution under the specified approximations.
sources.limits: The complex amplitude denotes classical inclination and phase. No quantum measurement postulate for stellar orbits follows. Applies to small inclinations and nearly Keplerian disks, not arbitrary galaxy halos.

sources.title: Eigenstates of Quasi-Keplerian Self-Gravitating Particle Discs
sources.locator: Sections 2-4; Tables 3-4; discussion of conserved inner product and imaginary-time evolution
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; abstract, mode comparisons and discussion read
sources.supports: The nonlocal classical coupling problem has a conserved inner product. Local approximations can fit mode shapes while failing on frequencies.
sources.limits: A correspondence in linear dynamics is weaker than physical equivalence of the systems; accuracy deteriorates with disk width and shorter wavelengths.

sources.title: Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter
sources.locator: Section III.2, equation 29 and its footnote; Appendix B
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; equation 29 and its qualification read
sources.supports: For the spherical time-independent Schrodinger-Poisson system, the half-mass radius bound has coefficient 3.925 and is saturated by the minimum-energy soliton.
sources.limits: The gravitating mass is the cloud itself. The inverse-mass radius relation does not imply a hydrogen spectrum or confirm fuzzy dark matter. The full real scalar field lacks exact particle-number conservation.

sources.title: Critical Exponents in 3.99 Dimensions
sources.locator: Publisher abstract: first-order epsilon expansion for Ising and XY susceptibility exponents
sources.access: Primary publisher abstract read; full article was subscription restricted
sources.supports: Renormalization-group analysis predicts differing critical exponents for different order-parameter symmetries near four dimensions.
sources.limits: The source's displayed calculation is perturbative in small epsilon. The report does not treat a first-order extrapolation to three dimensions as a precision prediction.

sources.title: Precision Islands in the Ising and O(N) Models
sources.locator: Abstract and stated 3D Ising/O(2)/O(3) scaling-data scope
sources.supports: Several distinct scaling dimensions and operator-product coefficients characterize a critical model beyond one matched exponent.
sources.limits: No new bootstrap calculation was performed here; applicability of a lattice model to a universality class still requires its assumptions.

sources.title: Dissipation of Energy in the Locally Isotropic Turbulence
sources.locator: 1991 English translation of 1941 paper, equations 5-7 and discussion of local isotropy and separation from the integral scale
sources.access: Primary paper in university-hosted scan; relevant derivation read
sources.supports: The signed longitudinal third-order increment relation is constrained by energy balance in the appropriate isotropic inertial-range limit.
sources.limits: Stationarity/local-stationarity, homogeneity, isotropy and scale separation matter. It does not fix all higher moments or imply exact self-similarity of probability distributions.

sources.title: An Optimal Shell Model of Turbulence (published as Improved shell model of turbulence)
sources.locator: Equation 16; structure functions and invariant-dependent oscillatory term
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; equation 16 and surrounding definitions read
sources.supports: The Sabra shell model has a model-specific third-order relation determined by two invariant fluxes.
sources.limits: Agreement with this exact identity tests the model calculation. The shell model omits spatial geometry and is not a validated model of every turbulent medium.

sources.title: Observation of Universality in Decaying Turbulence (author manuscript; published as Universal velocity statistics in decaying turbulence)
sources.access: Primary author manuscript read for full-function collapse versus power-law behavior
sources.supports: The reported high-Reynolds-number decaying-flow statistics approach a scale-dependent common form without a clean pure power law over the measured range.
sources.limits: The report confines the result to the described flow class and measurements. It does not establish the same universal function across all turbulence.

sources.title: Periodic tilings and auxetic deployments
sources.access: Publisher metadata read; full author manuscript retrieved from NSF and Section 7 extracted locally. Smith download returned 403, web NSF fetch returned 502, direct curl to the public NSF URL succeeded.
sources.supports: Bridged cross-polytope framework family exists in arbitrary dimension; 3D example uses octahedra and describes folding with a specified bar-to-edge ratio.
sources.limits: Does not establish the local repository's specific equal-bar non-overlapping fcc curve, physical stability, or material phase transition.

sources.title: A remarkable periodic solution of the three-body problem in the case of equal masses
sources.locator: Author abstract and published-version metadata, Annals of Mathematics 152 (2000), 881-901
sources.access: Primary author abstract read; not a re-verification of its variational proof
sources.supports: Existence of an equal-mass Newtonian figure-eight choreography with rich symmetry.
sources.limits: Existence is separate from a catalogue count, robustness to arbitrary perturbations, or astrophysical occurrence.

sources.title: Computer assisted proofs for non-symmetric planar choreographies and for stability of the Eight
sources.locator: Abstract; Introduction equations 1.1-1.3 and symmetry-reduction discussion
sources.access: Primary author PDF read for proof formulation and scope
sources.supports: Choreographies are fixed points of evolution plus permutation; translation, rotation, rescaling and phase symmetries must be reduced for isolated-root certification. Planar linear stability is a distinct checked property.
sources.limits: No existing orbit certificate was rerun in this research pass. The report's Newtonian scaling relation is an elementary derivation from the equations.

sources.title: Understanding critical collapse of a scalar field
sources.locator: Abstract; Sections II and IV; Table 2 convergence and perturbation spectrum
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; echoing, growing-mode and mass-scaling claims read
sources.supports: A discretely self-similar spherical massless-scalar critical solution has echoing period about 3.4453 and one growing perturbation mode, leading to mass exponent about 0.374 and a log-periodic correction.
sources.limits: Numerical classical gravity result, not an observed astrophysical echo. It is not automatically a model of halo formation, realistic stellar collapse, or quantum gravity.

sources.title: Observation of the Second Triatomic Resonance in Efimov's Scenario
sources.locator: Publisher abstract: measured scaling factor 21.0(1.3), ideal identical-boson value 22.7
sources.access: Primary publisher abstract read; full article was subscription restricted
sources.supports: Two cesium triatomic resonances with a finite-temperature analysis support discrete Efimov scaling.
sources.limits: Measurement is through recombination resonances and model analysis; it does not directly image an infinite tower of states.

sources.title: Geometric scaling of Efimov states in a 6Li-133Cs mixture
sources.locator: Primary author abstract; three successive resonances and measured ratio 4.9(4) versus 4.88 prediction
sources.supports: A changed constituent mass ratio changes the predicted and observed discrete scaling factor, supplying a control-response test.
sources.limits: Resonant cold-atom few-body regime. No common microscopic mechanism with gravitational collapse is inferred.

sources.title: Nonlinear Measures for Characterizing Rough Surface Morphologies
sources.locator: Sections IV.2-IV.3, equations 37-38; distinction between loops and level sets
sources.access: Primary author manuscript; derivation scope and explicit conjecture read
sources.supports: Individual contour-loop geometry differs from the whole level set. The general loop-dimension formula uses a conjectured loop-correlation exponent, exact in stated endpoint cases.
sources.limits: Gaussian/self-affine surface assumptions and observable definitions matter. Numerical agreement of cloud-outline dimensions is not enough to infer a shared mechanism.

own_inferences_and_probes.claim: The cab-to-fcc curve preserves its degree-5 contact graph throughout 0<s<1, then has degree-12 contacts at s=1.
own_inferences_and_probes.method: Exact integer-pair Bernstein coefficients prove strict positive separation for 6120 directed nonbar polynomials, and identify 30 directed bar identities. The analytic distant-image bound is inherited from the source proof. Endpoint contacts are counted with integers.
own_inferences_and_probes.limits: This reuses an existing unreviewed curve and its analytic bound. It is not a physical transition prediction or a new universal principle.

own_inferences_and_probes.claim: Fixed-J scalar Ising and fixed-p percolation on corresponding original bar graphs remain invariant under the geometric fold.
own_inferences_and_probes.derivation: The Hamiltonian or bond/site probability measure has no geometric parameter when graph, couplings and graph boundary conditions are fixed.
own_inferences_and_probes.limits: This invariance is built into the model. Physical distance correlations, scattering, geometry-selected boundaries, vector elasticity and microscopic couplings can change.

own_inferences_and_probes.claim: The bar and all-fcc-contact Ising models differ in high-temperature coefficients and ground-state energy.
own_inferences_and_probes.derivation: Even-subgraph expansion gives logZ/N = log2 + z K^2/4 + triangles_per_site K^3 + O(K^4). Counts yield (1.25,4/3) for original bars and (3,8) for full contacts. Ground energies are -2.5J and -6J per site.
own_inferences_and_probes.limits: Infinite simple-graph limit or sufficiently large periodic supercells; no small-torus edge identifications. Ferromagnetic uniform J, zero field. No Tc calculated.

own_inferences_and_probes.claim: Classical disk waves, gravitational atoms and self-gravitating solitons share useful mathematical forms without sharing all observables or mechanisms.
own_inferences_and_probes.limits: A useful mapping must specify operators, domains, boundary conditions, state interpretation, conserved norm and measured observables.

own_inferences_and_probes.claim: Discrete scale repetition and its response to an independent control are a promising bridge between few-body physics and critical dynamics.
own_inferences_and_probes.limits: Different physical equations and scales. No unified mechanism or matched numerical constant is proposed.

checks: Exact graph degree remains 5 at all declared geometric states
Exact nonbar separation throughout open parameter interval, conditional on analytic infinite-image bound
Integer endpoint coordinates give 12 contacts per site
Direct neighbor-pair enumeration gives 8 versus 48 triangles per six-site cell
Sampled bar squared-length error stays below 1e-12
Repository nextOrder(2,1,1,alpha,0.9) gives -0.010025 at alpha=0.1 and -0.079425 at alpha=0.3
Exact near-cancelling integer-pair signs verified against Pell pairs
A curve mutation that changes a bridge length is rejected
verification.limits: No raw astronomical-data fit, new physical measurement, finite-size Monte Carlo campaign, full orbit certification or new collapse evolution was performed.
